answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks via graph trust propagation from a seed crystal of vetted anchors. Verifiers run bounded random walks over peer endorsements to score each agent, giving cloned clusters behind sparse attack edges a weak trust signal. Because vouching slots are capped and standing grows like a glacier, attackers incur verifiable acquisition costs for trusted links per accepted identity instead of minting free bots. However, isolated newcomers face cold-start exclusion.
